newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Replacing Alitalia would aid Malev development - APV.
newsitem.headline: Replacing Alitalia would aid Malev development - APV.

text.p: Hungary's privatisation agency APV said on Wednesday it had advised the government to buy out Alitalia's 30 percent stake in national air carrier Malev Rt because Alitalia's domestic troubles would prevent it from focusing on Malev's development.

"Alitalia is temporarily in such a difficult position that we cannot expect it to take Malev in the strategic direction we would like to," APV managing director Benedek Belecz told Reuters. "Alitalia has problems with restructuring and it has some difficulties with the European Union."
Italy has been awaiting EU permission since last year for a capital injection worth 3.3 trillion lire ($1.9 billion) into Alitalia to prepare it for eventual privatisation.
The carrier's managing director Domenico Cempella later said the EU Commission had requested a reduction to 2.8 trillion.
Belecz said he believed the EU had already come to a decision on the matter but could not say what it was.
Alitalia bought a 30 percent stake in Malev in 1992. However, Belecz said the sale had not brought about expected developments.
"The hopes concerning privatisation did not come true," he said. APV would like to seek new strategic investors, pending government approval.
"It would be impossible to bring in another strategic investor in addition to Alitalia," Belecz said.

Earlier on Wednesday APV said it planned to start negotiations with Alitalia as soon as the government approved the plan, hopefully by the end of June and to complete the buyout by the end of the year.
APV also said it planned to list Malev on the Budapest Stock Exchange in 1998 or 1999.
Malev has a registered capital of 7.69 billion forints.
-- Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040 ($ = 1700 Italian Lire)
